This is SFCC-91 Step 3 of 4, REWORK round 2 (following your own round-1 REWORK verdict, which found a 🔴 pagination/selection blocker plus two 🟡 should-fix items in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/`). Do not commit, do not stage — read/investigate freely.

## Your own round-1 verdict, for reference (you wrote this)

REWORK, three defects:
1. 🔴 Blocker: `pageStart` always initialized to 0, so a selection beyond page 1 rendered on the wrong page with zero items checked and zero items tabbable (empirically reproduced by you, live, with your own from-scratch repro test — 6 populated colours, selection on the 6th, result: 4 rendered, 0 checked, 0 tabbable). You required the fix to handle BOTH initial mount AND resync if `selectedValue` changes on an already-mounted instance (explicitly warning that a mount-only fix would be insufficient, since Step 4 will eventually drive `selectedValue` as a live prop), plus a REQUIRED new test proving the on-mount case with no interaction.
2. 🟡 Should-fix: `index.tsx:156`'s comment cited "overrideStyling.md's 'your call' allowance" — confirmed by you via direct grep, this phrase exists nowhere in the rules docs. Instructed: remove the false citation, state the real reasoning plainly.
3. 🟡 Should-fix: Figma's truncation behaviour (correctly implemented) had zero regression coverage. Instructed: add a test with a long name asserting the truncation triad.

## What happened since, and what I (the orchestrating session) independently verified myself just now — not just accepted from the implementer's report

I read the actual current file content directly (not a diff, since the file is untracked and `git diff` shows nothing for untracked files — confirmed via `git status --porcelain`, which still shows only `M overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` and `?? .../zimmColourSwatchGroup/`, i.e. nothing else touched).

**Fix 1 — read directly, lines ~108-127 of the current `index.tsx`:**
```tsx
const selectedIndex = populated.findIndex((value) => value.value === selectedValue);
const selectedPageStart =
  selectedIndex === -1 ? 0 : Math.floor(selectedIndex / SWATCHES_PER_PAGE) * SWATCHES_PER_PAGE;

const [pageStart, setPageStart] = useState(selectedPageStart);

useEffect(() => {
  setPageStart(selectedPageStart);
}, [selectedPageStart]);
```
`selectedPageStart` is a plain derived value recomputed every render from `populated`/`selectedValue` (props), never itself stored state — so it can't independently drift. `useState(selectedPageStart)` seeds the correct page on first render (React only consumes a `useState` argument on mount). The `useEffect` keyed on `selectedPageStart` re-fires and resyncs `pageStart` whenever a prop change moves the selection to a different page on an already-mounted instance — satisfying your explicit "not mount-only" requirement. Manual `handlePrevPage`/`handleNextPage` only ever call `setPageStart` directly and never touch `selectedPageStart`, so the effect does not fire on a manual page click and manual paging is structurally unaffected. The in-file comments explain precisely why base SFCC's mount-only precedent isn't safe to copy here (base's `isFocusable` is derived fresh from props every render regardless of its own mount-only effect, since it only ever affects a highlight on already-rendered items; here `pageStart` gates which items are even rendered at all) — this is the exact distinction you yourself drew in round 1.

The implementer also reported building a throwaway `rerender`-based test (mount on a page-1 selection, `rerender` with a page-2 selection, confirm the visible page actually follows) and getting a real pass, then deleting it per the task's own instruction to do so. I did not personally re-run that exact rerender scenario myself this round — flagging this so you can decide whether to spot-check it yourself before trusting it, or judge the static code reasoning above sufficient on its own (the effect's dependency-array mechanics are deterministic and don't require empirical proof to verify by reading, unlike the original bug which required an empirical reproduction to even notice).

**Fix 2 — read directly, lines ~179-186:**
```
The label-group (the two "Colour:"/name text pieces) has no dedicated recipe part —
...
structural, one-off layout wrapper with no competing or interactive style definitions of
its own, so overrideStyling.md's "one canonical styling surface per component type" rule
— scoped to components with competing/interactive style definitions — does not clearly
[apply here...]
```
I independently grepped `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` myself, case-insensitively (my first case-sensitive attempt missed it, corrected) — line 89 is literally `## One canonical styling surface per component type`, a real section heading, and its actual content (also directly in my context) does center on interactive components with state-dependent styling (`_hover`/`_active`/`_focusVisible` etc.) that a static CSS class "can't express" — so the new comment's characterization is an accurate, defensible reading of a real rule, not a repeat fabrication. `grep -n "your call"` on the current file returns nothing — confirmed by me directly.

**Fix 3 — confirmed present.** `index.test.tsx:168`: `test('truncates a long selected colour name, and only the dynamic name — never the static "Colour:" label', ...)`. I read this test's body: it renders a 70-character `selectedName`, asserts via `getComputedStyle` that the dynamic name element has `overflow:'hidden'`, `textOverflow:'ellipsis'`, `whiteSpace:'nowrap'`, and separately asserts the static "Colour:" label's `textOverflow` is NOT `'ellipsis'`.

**All ten tests now in the file** (I listed them myself via grep): the original 8 plus `index.test.tsx:132` (`'mounts directly on the page containing the actual selection, not always page 1 (pagination regression)'`) and `:168` (the truncation test) — matching exactly what was required.

**Verification commands, re-run by the implementer and reported (I have not re-executed these myself this round — noting this explicitly rather than implying I did):** `tsc` 0 errors; scoped test file 10/10 passing; full suite 28 files/428 tests (426 + 2 new); lint and audit:tokens confirmed byte-identical to baseline via a stash/pop round-trip comparison; final `grep -n "your call"` empty.

## Your job

You may re-run any of the above yourself if you want first-hand confirmation rather than relying on my read — I've told you plainly which parts I verified directly (the file contents, the citation, the test presence) versus which I'm relying on the implementer's own report for (the exact command outputs, the deleted rerender-based resync proof). Re-score against your six axes and issue a final verdict. If PASS: state explicitly whether this step is ready to commit, or whether a visual checkpoint is still owed before that — and if so, exactly what should be checked and against what (this component has no live PDP caller yet, same situation as Step 2's atom, so weigh whether Storybook alone is sufficient here or not, and why, the same way you reasoned through Step 2's equivalent question).

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe for the PDP colour-swatch group — the "Colour: Bay Blue" label row, and (when there is
5	 * more than one populated colour) the row of ZimmColourSwatch rectangles beneath it. This recipe
6	 * only lays the group out; each swatch's own fill/border/focus styling stays in the sibling
7	 * ZimmColourSwatch atom's own recipe.
8	 *
9	 * Values below are read directly off Figma for this exact component, not estimated — node
10	 * 40000307:13867 ("ColourOptions"), within Zimmermann_Design_System_2026.
11	 *
12	 * Six parts:
13	 *   - `root` — outer vertical flex container: the label row above, the swatches row below.
14	 *   - `label` — the label row ("labelContainer" in Figma): the label-group (the two
15	 *     "Colour:"/name text pieces — laid out via a plain Chakra-prop wrapper in the component
16	 *     itself, not a seventh part here; see index.tsx's own comment for why) plus the pagination
17	 *     controls, right-aligned purely via the label-group's own `flex: 1 0 0` rather than an
18	 *     absolute-position hack.
19	 *   - `labelName` — the dynamic colour-name text specifically (e.g. "Bay Blue"). Gets its own
20	 *     part, unlike the static "Colour:" piece beside it, because it alone carries the
21	 *     Figma-mandated truncation behaviour: "If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation"
22	 *     (this node's own interaction annotation).
23	 *   - `swatches` — the horizontal row of rendered ZimmColourSwatch children.
24	 *   - `pagination` — wrapper around the two chevron buttons.
25	 *   - `pageButton` — each individual chevron button (24x24, holding a 16px ZimmIcon).
26	 */
27	export const ZimmColourSwatchGroup = {
28	  parts: ['root', 'label', 'labelName', 'swatches', 'pagination', 'pageButton'],
29	
30	  baseStyle: {
31	    root: {
32	      display: 'flex',
33	      flexDirection: 'column',
34	      // 8px between the label row and the swatches row. No background here — background lives
35	      // per-swatch, already handled by the atom's own recipe.
36	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
37	    },
38	
39	    label: {
40	      display: 'flex',
41	      alignItems: 'center',
42	      // 24px. Matches spacing.xl exactly, so the named step is used rather than the numerically
43	      // identical --zimm-scale-600 alias — see bottomBar.css.ts's own `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`
44	      // usage for the same 24px value elsewhere in this codebase.
45	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
46	      // 8px between the label-group and the pagination controls.
47	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
48	    },
49	
50	    labelName: {
51	      textStyle: 'caption',
52	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
53	      // The truncating half of the label-group's two text pieces (the static "Colour:" text
54	      // beside it never truncates — see index.tsx). `flex: 1 0 0` lets it consume the
55	      // label-group's remaining width; `minWidth: 0` is required for a flex item to actually
56	      // shrink below its content size instead of overflowing; the rest is the standard
57	      // single-line-ellipsis triad.
58	      flex: '1 0 0',
59	      minWidth: 0,
60	      overflow: 'hidden',
61	      textOverflow: 'ellipsis',
62	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
63	    },
64	
65	    swatches: {
66	      display: 'flex',
67	      width: '100%',
68	      // Confirmed directly off the Figma export, not a stylistic default: the 4-swatch example
69	      // measures exactly 192px total width for four 48px-wide swatches (4 x 48, no gap
70	      // contribution) — swatches sit directly adjacent. Do not add a gap here; that would be a
71	      // real deviation from the design, not a stylistic default.
72	      gap: 0,
73	    },
74	
75	    pagination: {
76	      display: 'flex',
77	      alignItems: 'center',
78	      // No inter-button gap value exists in the Figma export handed to this step — left at the
79	      // flex default (no `gap` declared at all) rather than invented. Revisit if a designer
80	      // confirms a real value.
81	    },
82	
83	    pageButton: {
84	      display: 'flex',
85	      alignItems: 'center',
86	      justifyContent: 'center',
87	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
88	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
89	      // Resets the native <button> UA chrome so the box is exactly the 24x24 the design calls
90	      // for, with the 16px ZimmIcon centred inside it by the flex alignment above.
91	      padding: 0,
92	      border: 'none',
93	      background: 'none',
94	      cursor: 'pointer',
95	      // No confirmed Figma spec for a disabled visual treatment on this control — same "leave an
96	      // unspecified visual state alone rather than invent one" precedent as swatch-group's own
97	      // disabled colour logic (see this codebase's Known Gaps notes). The native `disabled`
98	      // attribute (set in index.tsx) already makes the control genuinely inert and announces as
99	      // disabled to assistive tech; only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX
100	      // keyword, not a design token.
101	      _disabled: {
102	        cursor: 'not-allowed',
103	      },
104	      // Same uniform ring every other interactive control in ui-kits/ uses (zimmColourSwatch,
105	      // zimmNavItem) — --zimm-focus-ring already composites the border-width/colour pair.
106	      _focusVisible: {
107	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
108	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
109	      },
110	    },
111	  } satisfies Record<string, SystemStyleObject>,
112	};

11	**The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor.** An earlier version of this memory said

16	  cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts: "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs
17	  18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
18	- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — so a delta here is a
19	  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against our 45/68 was a real gap, and the
20	  naive "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.
21	
22	**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is a
23	defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the heading's
24	cap box.
25	
26	**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, deriving from `lineHeight` +
27	4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

29	**There are TWO Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like from one:**
30	`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).

33	`Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap change 40→24: the
34	design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix that suppressed intended
35	growth when the 68px padded box was already design-correct.

37	**Frames are not breakpoints.** Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024.
38	The unframed **768–1022 band was genuinely broken** (18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels) and
39	covers three iPad models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking* — the

43	`theme.sizes` (36rem) blew contact icons to 576px and destroyed the footer on every page while

metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f5f727b4-7546-4aa6-9d86-ef229e247d3f
  modified: 2026-08-22T14:05:00.000Z
---

**The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor.** An earlier version of this memory said
simply "Figma reports the glyph box, CSS reports the line box." That's only true of **text nodes**,
and the missing half is what makes the rule usable:

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`, `text-box-edge:
  cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts: "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs
  18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — so a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against our 45/68 was a real gap, and the
  naive "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is a
defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the heading's
cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, deriving from `lineHeight` +
4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

**There are TWO Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like from one:**
`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page file
produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states" (actually
`Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap change 40→24: the
design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix that suppressed intended
growth when the 68px padded box was already design-correct.

**Frames are not breakpoints.** Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024.
The unframed **768–1022 band was genuinely broken** (18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels) and
covers three iPad models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking* — the
row refused to break so the words broke instead.

**No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect.** `width: 'xl'` resolving through
`theme.sizes` (36rem) blew contact icons to 576px and destroyed the footer on every page while
passing tsc, eslint, vitest, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and Storybook a11y. Only rendering
beside Figma found it.

**Method notes:** measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports frame-relative
coordinates); use `domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server; dismiss the consent
banner first; `Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point;
`document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families and is useless — compare widths
instead; and **mutation-test layout fixes at mobile**, since two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only
because a taller sibling column masked them.

**How to apply:** before calling any Figma-vs-code delta an artifact, check the node type. Text →
likely artifact, verify uniformity. Frame or instance → treat as real. See
[[feedback-prove-dont-assert]] and [[project-chakra-scale-registration]].

18	    swatch: {
19	      display: 'inline-block',

22	      // nothing between 64px and 140px — so it's expressed as an aspect ratio on the width
